title: Direct Acceleration of Stochastic Root-Finding Without Variance Reduction and Regularization
claim: Our method steadily reduces residual norm per sample budget, competing with or beating stochastic baselines across worst-case and finite-sum settings.
layout: 2 side-by-side log-scale line plots, shared legend style, shaded percentile bands
description: Two side-by-side line plots on a log-scale y-axis showing residual norm ||F(x_k)|| against sample count (0 to 2000). The left panel, x-axis 'stochastic oracle samples', covers a worst-case nonexpansive construction. The proposed S-Dual-OHM, a dark blue solid line, starts high and declines slowly, then drops sharply near 2000 samples to about 0.1. The baselines are S-OHM (Const B), Halpern-PAGE, RAIN, SGDA and SEG. They drop faster early on and plateau or flatten at higher values. The right panel, x-axis 'component-operator calls', covers a finite-sum cocoercive setting. All methods decay with shaded 5th-95th percentile bands. S-Dual-OHM ends near 0.09, while SGDA ends lower, around 0.05. Halpern-PAGE and Halpern-VR-Finite stall at high values. A legend sits in the upper right of each panel. Colors are distinct per method, with varied markers and dash styles.
caption: Plot of residual norm versus stochastic samples. (Left) Worst-case nonexpansive operator construction (Experiment 1). (Right) Finite-sum random cocoercive operator construction (Experiment 2). Solid curves indicate means over 10 independent runs, and shaded bands denote empirical 5th--95th percentiles.
abstract: Acceleration for deterministic root-finding problems has been extensively studied in recent years; specifically, the anchor-based, or Halpern-type methods achieve optimal convergence rates with respect to the operator norm. However, acceleration via these methods does not directly carry over to stochastic setting due to accumulation of errors, unless one enforces diminishing variance via increasing batch sizes or variance reduction techniques. In this work, we show that another class of acceleration, namely the dual-anchor mechanism, extends to the stochastic setting without such error accumulation, in contrast to anchor-based algorithms. Consequently, we cleanly achieve $O(Îµ^{-3})$ complexity with iteration-independent batch size, without any variance reduction or double-loop recursive regularization, for stochastic root-finding (resp. fixed-point) problems with cocoercivity (resp. square-nonexpansivity) in expectation. For strongly monotone operators, the same algorithm attains a sharper $\widetilde{O} (Îµ^{-2})$ complexity, nearly matching the lower bound in terms of $Îµ$-dependence.
